name: Benfotiamine
short: In placebo-controlled trials lasting up to 12 months, adverse events were similar to placebo. In short phase I studies, raised ALT (a liver enzyme) was a commonly reported drug-related event.
text: In two phase I placebo-controlled trials in healthy subjects, the incidence and severity of adverse events were similar with benfotiamine and placebo; the commonly reported drug-related events were a raised liver enzyme (ALT) and white blood cells in the urine. In a 12-month randomised trial in 57 people with type 2 diabetes and neuropathy, there were no relevant differences from placebo in the rates of adverse events, and a twelve-month placebo-controlled trial in 70 people with mild cognitive impairment or mild Alzheimer's dementia reported the treatment as safe. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
